joel: Heads-up — following the RFC: we need to resolve the signer-lease renewal handshake for air-gapped bundles. Current problem: when we rotate signing keys for onprem distributors, nodes without connectivity can end up rejecting new bundles because their verifier rejects unknown signer epochs. How tolerant should the verifier be?

tara: +1. My quick take: support a short dual-accept window where verifiers accept both the previous signer epoch and the new one for N hours after rotation. Operator-triggered renewal (manual accept) should be possible for long-lived airgapped fleets. :thinking_face:

simon: Tradeoffs: dual-accept simplifies rollout but increases attack surface if old key is compromised. We can constrain by scoping the dual window to signed-lease metadata and require a signed-epoch-rotation record that itself is chained to the old signer. That gives cryptographic continuity instead of blind acceptance.

anna: Also consider time drift. Many airgapped clusters have no reliable NTP. We should avoid any design that requires accurate clocks. Suggestion: use monotonic epoch counters + sequence numbers in manifests rather than absolute expiry timestamps. Verifier logic: prefer latest epoch if chain-valid, otherwise accept previous epoch up to sequence gap G.

joel: Good point about clocks. So proposal sketch: (1) signing service emits signed-rotation-entry that includes new_epoch_id, prev_epoch_id, rotation_seq, and optional grace_duration. (2) verifier accepts new_epoch if rotation entry verifies against prev key OR if operator has explicitly approved new_epoch locally.

tara: UX: operator approval can be via an encrypted USB token or short-lived operator-signed certificate that gets physically delivered. Keep the local approval primitive simple: a CLI command `redwood-accept-epoch --token <file>` that writes a local trust anchor.

simon: Pseudocode for acceptance check:```
# verifier acceptance rules
if verify_chain(manifest.signed_by_epoch, local_trust_anchor):
  accept
elif local_operator_approved_epoch(manifest.epoch):
  accept
elif manifest.rotation_entry.chain_valid_against(local_trust_anchor) and manifest.rotation_seq - local_seq <= MAX_GAP:
  accept
else:
  reject
```
This avoids relying on wall clock while bounding how far ahead a new epoch can jump.

anna: Edge case: emergency key revocation. If we revoke prev_key, nodes in the field may still have cached prev_key and accept malicious rollforward. Mitigation: include revocation markers in a short 'revocation bundle' that operators deliver physically; verifier prioritizes revocation lists if present. Also keep a signed revocation_txn that references rotation_seq so we can correlate.

joel: Operational flow for rotation then: publish rotation_entry -> deliver rotation_entry to private airgap channel (or operator) -> operator runs local accept or provides token -> nodes update local_seq and start accepting new epoch. If revocation needed, operator pushes revocation bundle and we prohibit any rotation entries that chain from revoked_seq.

tara: Agree. Also add telemetry: when a node starts accepting a new epoch, log a local event with the rotation_seq and operator id for audit. We'll surface those in Console when the private control plane syncs.

simon: One more detail: while dual-accept window exists, we should require that any bundle signed by the new epoch includes a 'rotation_proof' that contains the previous epoch signature over the new epoch id. That binds them cryptographically and limits blind acceptance.

anna: Implementation note: keep verifier logic as stateless as possible; store only latest_seq, allowed_local_approvals, and a small revocation_set. All other checks are pure crypto verify against stored keys. That helps with small devices with limited storage.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] note: added issue #A-1423 to track RFC follow-up (signer-lease UX + offline approval primitives).

joel: Nice. Can someone capture this as an RFC follow-up section (rotation flow, local approval primitive, revocation bundle format, verifier pseudocode)? I'll sketch and ping for review. :memo:

tara: I'll take the write-up for operator UX + CLI examples.

simon: I'll draft the verifier pseudocode and threat model section.

anna: I'll cover revocation semantics and compact revocation bundle format.

joel: Perfect — aiming to have a draft by EOD Friday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
